text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Vascular neurology consultation in two weeks, with carotid duplex ultrasound before it, for a right carotid bruit in a man with high blood pressure: degree of stenosis, medical therapy or revascularization, and surveillance
  • Home blood pressure monitoring twice daily for seven days with a validated upper-arm cuff, to confirm or exclude hypertension before treatment; lower salt, the DASH eating pattern, and daily walking
  • Baseline tests: basic metabolic panel, HbA1c, lipid panel, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, TSH, hemoglobin and ALT, and a resting ECG; re-entry screening with a hepatitis C antibody, an interferon-gamma release assay for latent tuberculosis, an HIV test and a hepatitis B panel; PHQ-9
  • Re-entry support: a release-of-information request for his prison medical records, a social work referral for housing, Social Security and Medicare enrollment, a low-cost pharmacy plan, and a conversation about shame and reputation, with follow-up of mood at each visit
  • Two first-line drugs for stage 2 hypertension, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and amlodipine 5 mg daily, aiming for below 130/80 mmHg, with sodium, potassium and creatinine in about four weeks
  • Best medical therapy for asymptomatic right carotid stenosis of 50 to 69 percent: atorvastatin 40 mg and aspirin 81 mg daily, a lipid panel and ALT in 4 to 12 weeks, blood pressure control, stroke warning signs and calling 911, and a repeat duplex in twelve months
  • Switch hydrochlorothiazide to losartan 50 mg daily after a drug-induced gout flare, with potassium and creatinine one to two weeks after starting; no urate-lowering drug after a single flare

resource.title: Frederick Cook synthetic care plan
resource.description: Re-entry primary care for a 65-year-old former physician and explorer establishing care four months after release from about six years in prison: medication reconciliation without records; high blood pressure at the first visit confirmed with home readings (stage 2 hypertension, two first-line drugs under the 1929 AHA/ACC guideline, target below 130/80); a right carotid bruit evaluated with duplex ultrasound, which finds an asymptomatic 50 to 69 percent internal carotid stenosis managed with best medical therapy (a statin, low-dose aspirin, blood pressure control and yearly surveillance) rather than revascularization, and stroke warning signs; a drug-induced gout flare on hydrochlorothiazide, treated with low-dose colchicine and followed by a switch to losartan under the 1924 ACR gout guideline; hepatitis C, latent tuberculosis, HIV and hepatitis B screening after incarceration (USPSTF and CDC); depression and shame screening; housing, income, benefits and reputation as health needs; and the Welcome to Medicare preventive examination with vaccinations. Built on the 1929 AHA/ACC hypertension guideline, the 1928 AHA/ASA primary stroke prevention guideline, the SVS 1925 and ESVS 1927 carotid guidelines, the 1922 AHA/ACC cholesterol guideline, the CMID hypertension, hyperlipidemia and stroke monographs, the 1924 ACR gout guideline, and the USPSTF and CDC recommendations.
